text: At the beginning of the reign of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah, this word came from the LORD:

This is what the LORD says: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak to all who come from the cities of Judah to worship in the house of the LORD. Tell them everything I command you; do not hold back a single word.

versions.text: This is what the LORD says: Stand in the court of the LORD's house and speak to all the people of the cities of Judah who come to worship there. Tell them everything I command you; do not hold back a single word.
versions.explanation: "worship there" is vague after "the court of the LORD's house"; the Hebrew repeats "house of the LORD," and the phrasing "all who come from the cities of Judah" reads more naturally aloud while keeping the sense of the Hebrew.

text: Perhaps they will listen and each one turn from his evil way. Then I will relent of the disaster I intend to bring on them because of the evil of their deeds.
Say to them: This is what the LORD says: If you will not listen to me and walk in my law, which I have set before you,
and heed the words of my servants the prophets, whom I have sent to you again and again, though you have not listened,
then I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.
The priests, the prophets, and all the people heard Jeremiah speaking these words in the house of the LORD.
And when Jeremiah had finished saying everything the LORD had commanded him to say to all the people, the priests, the prophets, and all the people seized him and said, "You must die!

Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD that this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be desolate, without an inhabitant?" And all the people gathered against Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.

versions.text: Why have you prophesied in the name of the LORD that this house will become like Shiloh and this city will be desolate, without an inhabitant?" And all the people crowded around Jeremiah in the house of the LORD.
versions.explanation: The niphal of קהל with אֶל here carries a hostile sense in context (the crowd is threatening Jeremiah). "Crowded around" softens the menace; "gathered against" better conveys it.

text: When the officials of Judah heard of these things, they came up from the king's palace to the house of the LORD and took their seats at the entrance of the New Gate of the LORD's house.
Then the priests and the prophets said to the officials and to all the people, "This man deserves a sentence of death, for he has prophesied against this city, as you have heard with your own ears."
Then Jeremiah said to all the officials and all the people: "The LORD sent me to prophesy against this house and this city everything you have heard.
Now then, reform your ways and your deeds, and obey the voice of the LORD your God, and the LORD will relent of the disaster he has pronounced against you.
As for me, I am in your hands. Do with me whatever seems good and right to you.

But know for certain that if you put me to death, you will bring innocent blood on yourselves, on this city, and on its inhabitants; for in truth the LORD has sent me to you to speak all these words in your hearing."
Then the officials and all the people said to the priests and the prophets, "This man does not deserve a sentence of death, for he has spoken to us in the name of the LORD our God."
And some of the elders of the land rose and said to the whole assembly of the people:

"Micah of Moresheth prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah, and he said to all the people of Judah: 'This is what the LORD of hosts says: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem will become a heap of ruins, and the temple mount a wooded height.'

Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek his favor, so that the LORD relented of the disaster he had pronounced against them? But we would be bringing great harm on our own lives!

versions.text: Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him to death? Did he not fear the LORD and seek his favor, so that the LORD relented of the disaster he had pronounced against them? But we are about to bring a terrible disaster on ourselves!"
versions.explanation: The Hebrew participle with עַל־נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ speaks of the elders bringing guilt/harm upon their own lives (souls), not merely of future disaster. "On ourselves" loses the force of נַפְשׁוֹתֵינוּ, and "are about to" overstates the participle.

text: Now there was also a man named Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim, who prophesied in the name of the LORD. He prophesied against this city and this land in words just like Jeremiah's.

versions.text: Now there was another man who prophesied in the name of the LORD: Uriah son of Shemaiah from Kiriath-jearim. He prophesied against this city and this land in words exactly like Jeremiah's.
versions.explanation: The awkward mid-verse colon interrupts oral flow; also the Hebrew וְגַם is better rendered "also" than "another," and the name is introduced after the verb in Hebrew, which the smoother English word order preserves in sense.

text: When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and was afraid, so he fled and went to Egypt.

versions.text: When King Jehoiakim and all his warriors and all the officials heard his words, the king sought to put him to death. But Uriah heard of it and was afraid, so he fled and escaped to Egypt.
versions.explanation: The Hebrew says he fled and came/went to Egypt; "escaped" adds a nuance not in the text and is ironic given he was later brought back and killed.

text: Then King Jehoiakim sent men to Egypt: Elnathan son of Achbor and others with him.
They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who struck him down with the sword and threw his corpse into the burial place of the common people.

versions.text: They brought Uriah out of Egypt and took him to King Jehoiakim, who put him to the sword and threw his body into the burial place of the common people.
versions.explanation: נִבְלָתוֹ is a stronger word than "body" (corpse/carcass), conveying the indignity of the act; "struck him down with the sword" also renders וַיַּכֵּהוּ בֶּחָרֶב more precisely.

text: But Ahikam son of Shaphan gave Jeremiah his support, so that he was not handed over to the people to be put to death.
